tasks.title: Node NotReady: kubelet stopped
tasks.question:
ssh cka01001
The worker node node01 is reported as NotReady. Investigate the cause and bring node01 back to the Ready state. Your fix must survive a reboot of node01.
keys: fix must survive reboot (enable the service)
tasks.setup:
ssh node01 'systemctl stop kubelet; systemctl disable kubelet' 2>/dev/null
sleep 45
clear

steps.title: See which node is sick
steps.why: NotReady usually means the kubelet on that node is not talking.

steps.title: Log in to node01
steps.why: The kubelet runs on the node itself, not as a pod.

steps.title: Check the kubelet service
steps.why: Shows the kubelet is stopped and will not start at boot.

steps.title: Start it and enable it at boot
steps.why: enable = survives reboot, --now = start right away.

steps.title: Go back and check
steps.why: Wait up to 30s for the node to report Ready.

tasks.beginner: The kubelet program on node01 is switched off; turn it on and make it start automatically.

tasks.title: Service has no endpoints
tasks.question:

tasks.setup:

cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -

kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: cart, namespace: shop}
spec:
  replicas: 2

tasks.title: Pods stuck Pending (requests too big)
tasks.question:
ssh cka01003
The Pods of Deployment reporter in namespace batch stay Pending. Find the reason and fix it so that all replicas are Running. Set the memory request of the container to 128Mi. Keep the number of replicas unchanged.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace batch --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: reporter, namespace: batch}
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: reporter}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: reporter}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: reporter
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
        resources: {requests: {memory: 64Gi}}
EOF
clear

steps.title: See Pending pods
steps.why: Pending = scheduler cannot find a node.

steps.title: Read the reason
cmds: kubectl -n batch describe pod -l app=reporter | grep -A3 Events

steps.title: Lower the request
cmds: kubectl -n batch set resources deploy reporter --requests=memory=128Mi
steps.why: Asks for less memory so a node fits.

steps.title: Check
steps.why: New pods replace the old Pending ones.

tasks.title: CrashLoop / restarts: wrong liveness probe
tasks.question:
ssh cka01004
Deployment api in namespace web keeps restarting its Pods. Identify the cause and fix it. The nginx container listens on port 80. Do not delete the Deployment.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace web --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: api, namespace: web}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: api}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: api}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.27-alpine
        ports: [{containerPort: 80}]
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /, port: 8080}
          initialDelaySeconds: 3
          periodSeconds: 3
          failureThreshold: 2
EOF
clear

steps.title: See restarts
steps.why: Growing RESTARTS = something kills the container.

steps.title: Read events
cmds: kubectl -n web describe pod -l app=api | grep -i -A2 liveness
steps.why: Probe checks port 8080 but nginx uses 80.

steps.title: Fix the probe port
steps.why: Probe now checks the right port.

steps.title: Check
cmds: kubectl -n web rollout status deploy api
steps.why: New pod stays healthy.

tasks.docs: Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes (search: livenessProbe httpGet)
tasks.beginner: The health check knocks on the wrong door (8080) so Kubernetes keeps restarting the pod.

tasks.title: Gateway API: migrate Ingress to Gateway + HTTPRoute
tasks.question:
ssh cka01011
Migrate the existing Ingress web in namespace web-app to the Gateway API, keeping HTTPS:
- Create a Gateway named web-gateway using GatewayClass nginx, with an HTTPS listener on port 443 for hostname gateway.web.example. Use the TLS Secret web-tls already referenced by the Ingress.
- Create an HTTPRoute named web-route bound to web-gateway that sends all paths (/) for gateway.web.example to Service web on port 80.
- Delete the Ingress web when done.
keys: listener HTTPS 443, host gateway.web.example, secret web-tls
delete ingress web at the end
tasks.setup:
kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io >/dev/null 2>&1 || kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.2.1/standard-install.yaml
kubectl create namespace web-app --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
openssl req -x509 -nodes -newkey rsa:2048 -days 365 -subj "/CN=gateway.web.example" -keyout /tmp/web-tls.key -out /tmp/web-tls.crt 2>/dev/null
kubectl -n web-app create secret tls web-tls --cert=/tmp/web-tls.crt --key=/tmp/web-tls.key --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GatewayClass
metadata: {name: nginx}
spec: {controllerName: example.net/gateway-controller}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: web, namespace: web-app}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: web}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: web}}
    spec:
      containers: [{name: nginx, image: nginx:1.27-alpine, ports: [{containerPort: 80}]}]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: web, namespace: web-app}
spec: {selector: {app: web}, ports: [{port: 80, targetPort: 80}]}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata: {name: web, namespace: web-app}
spec:
  tls: [{hosts: [gateway.web.example], secretName: web-tls}]
  rules:
  - host: gateway.web.example
    http:
      paths:
      - {path: /, pathType: Prefix, backend: {service: {name: web, port: {number: 80}}}}
EOF
clear

steps.title: Read the Ingress you must copy
cmds: kubectl -n web-app get ingress web -o yaml | grep -A12 "^spec"
steps.why: Host, TLS secret and backend move to the new objects.

steps.title: Check the GatewayClass
steps.why: Gateway must use an existing class.

steps.title: Create the Gateway
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata: {name: web-gateway, namespace: web-app}
spec:
  gatewayClassName: nginx
  listeners:
  - name: https
    protocol: HTTPS
    port: 443
    hostname: gateway.web.example
    tls:
      mode: Terminate
      certificateRefs:
      - {kind: Secret, name: web-tls}
EOF
steps.why: Gateway = the entry door with TLS.

steps.title: Create the HTTPRoute
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: {name: web-route, namespace: web-app}
spec:
  parentRefs: [{name: web-gateway}]
  hostnames: [gateway.web.example]
  rules:
  - matches: [{path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}}]
    backendRefs: [{name: web, port: 80}]
EOF
steps.why: Route = which traffic goes to which Service.

steps.title: Delete the old Ingress
steps.why: Migration done; old object removed.

verify: kubectl -n web-app get gateway web-gateway -o yaml | grep -A8 listeners
kubectl -n web-app get httproute web-route -o yaml | grep -A6 rules
tasks.docs: kubernetes.io: Gateway API (search: HTTPRoute, Gateway listener tls certificateRefs); gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io HTTPS guide
tasks.beginner: Rebuild the HTTPS Ingress as a Gateway (door + certificate) and an HTTPRoute (path to service). No Gateway controller runs on Killercoda, so status stays Unknown - that is fine.

Create a new PriorityClass named urgent for user workloads. Its value must be exactly one less than the highest existing user-defined PriorityClass value (ignore the system-* classes).

tasks.title: HPA with scale-down behavior
tasks.question:
ssh cka01014
Create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler named apache-server in namespace autoscale for the existing Deployment apache-server. It must target 50% CPU utilisation per Pod, with a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 4 replicas. Set the scale-down stabilization window to 30 seconds.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace autoscale --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: apache-server, namespace: autoscale}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: apache-server}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: apache-server}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - {name: httpd, image: httpd:2.4-alpine, resources: {requests: {cpu: 100m}}}
EOF
clear

steps.title: Create the HPA (autoscaling/v2)
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata: {name: apache-server, namespace: autoscale}
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: {apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: apache-server}
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 4
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: cpu, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 50}}
  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 30
EOF
steps.why: behavior only exists in v2 YAML.

steps.title: Check it
steps.why: <unknown> just means no metrics-server; fine.

steps.title: Check the window
cmds: kubectl -n autoscale get hpa apache-server -o jsonpath="{.spec.behavior.scaleDown}"
steps.why: Proves behavior was saved.

verify: kubectl -n autoscale get hpa apache-server -o yaml | grep -A4 behavior
tasks.docs: kubernetes.io: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (search: stabilizationWindowSeconds behavior)

tasks.title: Reuse a retained PV for MariaDB
tasks.question:
ssh cka01016
A MariaDB Deployment in namespace mariadb was deleted by mistake, but its PersistentVolume mariadb-pv was kept.
- Create a PersistentVolumeClaim named mariadb in namespace mariadb: access mode ReadWriteOnce, storage 250Mi, so that it binds to the existing PV.
- Edit /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml so the Deployment uses this PVC, then apply it. Ensure the Pod is Running.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace mariadb --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: {name: mariadb-pv}
spec:
  capacity: {storage: 250Mi}
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: ""
  hostPath: {path: /mnt/data/mariadb, type: DirectoryOrCreate}
EOF
cat <<'EOF' > /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: mariadb, namespace: mariadb}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: mariadb}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: mariadb}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: mariadb
        image: mariadb:11
        env: [{name: MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD, value: cka}]
        volumeMounts: [{name: data, mountPath: /var/lib/mysql}]
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: ""
EOF
clear

steps.title: Look at the PV
steps.why: Note size, mode and empty class.

steps.title: Create the matching PVC
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: mariadb, namespace: mariadb}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: ""
  resources: {requests: {storage: 250Mi}}
EOF
steps.why: Empty class "" stops the default class grabbing it.

steps.title: Check it is Bound
steps.why: Bound to the old PV = old data kept.

apiVersion: apps/v1

spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: order-app}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: order-app}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: [sh, -c, "while true; do echo order $(date) >> /var/log/order.log; sleep 3; done"]

kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: order-app, namespace: logging}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: order-app}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: order-app}}
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: log-shipper
        image: busybox:1.36
        restartPolicy: Always
        command: [sh, -c, "tail -n+1 -F /var/log/order.log"]
        volumeMounts: [{name: logs, mountPath: /var/log}]
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: [sh, -c, "while true; do echo order $(date) >> /var/log/order.log; sleep 3; done"]

tasks.title: Gateway API: header match + weighted split
tasks.question:
ssh cka03010
In namespace shop-gw a Gateway shop-gw (HTTP, port 80) and Services shop-v1 and shop-v2 exist.
Create an HTTPRoute named shop-route attached to shop-gw for hostname shop.example.com:
- Requests with header x-version: v2 go 100% to shop-v2.
- All other requests are split 80% shop-v1 and 20% shop-v2.
Both Services listen on port 80.
tasks.setup:
kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io >/dev/null 2>&1 || kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.2.1/standard-install.yaml
kubectl create namespace shop-gw --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GatewayClass
metadata: {name: nginx}
spec: {controllerName: example.net/gateway-controller}
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata: {name: shop-gw, namespace: shop-gw}
spec:
  gatewayClassName: nginx
  listeners: [{name: http, protocol: HTTP, port: 80}]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: shop-v1, namespace: shop-gw}
spec: {selector: {app: shop, v: "1"}, ports: [{port: 80}]}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: shop-v2, namespace: shop-gw}
spec: {selector: {app: shop, v: "2"}, ports: [{port: 80}]}
EOF
clear

steps.title: Check the Gateway
cmds: kubectl -n shop-gw get gateway shop-gw -o yaml | grep -A3 listeners
steps.why: Route will attach to this.

steps.title: Create the HTTPRoute
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: {name: shop-route, namespace: shop-gw}
spec:
  parentRefs: [{name: shop-gw}]
  hostnames: [shop.example.com]
  rules:
  - matches:
    - headers: [{name: x-version, value: v2}]
    backendRefs: [{name: shop-v2, port: 80}]
  - matches:
    - path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}
    backendRefs:
    - {name: shop-v1, port: 80, weight: 80}
    - {name: shop-v2, port: 80, weight: 20}
EOF
steps.why: Header rule is more specific, so it wins.

steps.title: Check
cmds: kubectl -n shop-gw describe httproute shop-route | grep -A20 Rules
steps.why: Both rules stored correctly.

tasks.title: Re-bind a Released PV (clear claimRef)
tasks.question:
ssh cka03016
The PostgreSQL data PersistentVolume pg-data-pv still holds data, but it is in Released state after its old claim was deleted.
- Make the PV available again WITHOUT deleting it or its data.
- Create PVC pg-data in namespace postgres (1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, storageClassName manual) that binds to it.
- Deploy /root/pg-deploy.yaml (already uses claim pg-data) and make sure the Pod is Running.

kubectl get pv pg-data-pv >/dev/null 2>&1 || cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: {name: pg-data-pv}
spec:
  capacity: {storage: 1Gi}
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath: {path: /mnt/pg-data, type: DirectoryOrCreate}
  claimRef: {namespace: postgres, name: old-pg-claim, uid: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001}
EOF
cat <<'EOF' > /root/pg-deploy.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: postgres, namespace: postgres}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: postgres}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: postgres}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: postgres
        image: postgres:17-alpine
        env:
        - {name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD, value: cka}
        - {name: PGDATA, value: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata}
        volumeMounts: [{name: data, mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data}]
      volumes:
      - {name: data, persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: pg-data}}
EOF
sleep 5
clear
